According to arXiv 2608.25839, conflict zone capability transfers primarily affect the success rate of catastrophic terrorist attempts by improving operational capacity, while they do not substantially affect the attempt rate. This is because capability transfer enhances execution rather than motivation to attempt attacks. 

On the other hand, AI-assisted attack planning affects both the attempt rate and the success rate. AI lowers the knowledge barrier for attack planning, enabling more individuals to attempt attacks (increasing the attempt rate) and improving the quality of plans for those already motivated (increasing the success rate). However, the severity of harm remains constrained by execution barriers, as AI assistance does not eliminate the need for acquiring materials and deploying them without detection.
